added.title: Environmental Compliance Manager
added.description:
Thank you for considering a career at Port Houston. We appreciate your interest in joining our team. By applying, you are taking an important step toward advancing your career with an organization committed to excellence.

Port Houston offers competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and a diverse, inclusive work environment. Joining our team means embarking on a fulfilling career path with opportunities for growth and impact.

Before submitting your application, please ensure your resume is ready for upload in either .doc or .pdf format. Application must be completed in full.

Position Summary

Environmental Affairs Environmental Affairs Director Exempt G The Environmental Compliance Manager plays a pivotal leadership role within Port Houston’s Environmental Affairs team. The Environmental Compliance Manager will lead the team of coordinators through compliance, permitting, auditing, and a variety of other complicated environmental programs from cross functional disciplines including air, water, waste, sustainability, construction project oversight, remediation, tanks, spills, hazmat coordination, environmental permits, and regulatory oversight with various agencies (USACE, EPA, TCEQ, NEPA, etc). Provides subject matter and technical expertise in a minimum of four scientific disciplines, while managing contracts, budgets, and consultant work to achieve and sustain environmental initiatives.

Key Responsibilities/Duties

Develop, manage, and oversee environmental programs with and through the environmental compliance coordinators.
Examine Port Houston operations to identify process improvements and ensure compliance with environmental regulations across the organization
Manage day-to-day activities of the Environmental Compliance Coordinators
Support Port Houston’s efforts by ensuring permitting and compliance projects meet current environmental regulations and best practices and will service as a backup to the director of environmental affairs during his/her absence
Act as a mentor to the other Environmental Compliance Coordinators and is acting as an Environmental Affairs Director, as needed
Assist in developing a five- and ten-year strategic plan to minimize Port Houston’s environmental footprint in a sustainable fashion, develop metrics to track progress, and re-assess and report on progress annually
Develop scopes of work, negotiate contracts for professional environmental services, and manage environmental consultants
Oversee and manage highly complex permits, and contracts through legal requirements, project management, cost constraints and budgets
Coordinate business functions with the appropriate regulatory agencies to ensure that all required permitting is in place, and that permit limitations are compatible with business needs
Develop and implement environmental strategies and action plans
Assess and implement existing and proposed local, state and federal regulations
Assist with environmental compliance through education, training, implementation of corporate compliance and company initiatives
Serve as permit project manager for all non-marine, land-based environmental permits, including:
Nationwide Permits (NWP) under Section 404/10/401, with USACE when applicable
TCEQ permits and registrations (e.g., stormwater, remediation, air, waste).
EPA-regulated activities, such as spill prevention, hazardous materials, and site investigations
Monitor, interpret, track, and analyze proposed environmental, energy and related legislation, regulations, and policies at the federal, state, and local levels that could potentially adversely impact Port Houston or could significantly increase environmental compliance requirements and costs
Lead or support NEPA compliance processes, including Environmental Assessments (EA) and coordination of Environmental Impact Statements (EIS), when triggered by federal funding or agencies
Conduct and/or manage consultants for wetland delineations, biological surveys, and species/habitat impact assessments
Oversee Phase I, II, and III Environmental Site Assessments (ESAs) to support real estate, development, or remediation decisions
Promote and raise awareness at all organizational levels on the impact of emerging environmental issues
Conduct inspections, audits, and training to ensure implementation of best management practices, adherence to regulatory requirements, and promote continuous improvement
Demonstrate environmental compliance, maintain compliance records and document, and submit required reports and documents to various regulatory agencies within the required time limits
Perform data assessment and analysis of environmental data using GIS and other software
Serve as subject matter expert to assess impacts of the changes and actively participate in policy development through industry associations and direct integration with regulating agencies
Identify and prioritize potential environmental risks and develop appropriate control and/or abatement mechanisms
Research proposed local, state and federal regulatory changes; assess impacts of the changes and actively participate in rulemaking activities through industry associations and direct interaction with regulators; maintain liaison with agencies, NGO’s, other stakeholders
Coordinate and engage environmental personnel and other personnel in the identification, development and implementation of environmental goals which will positively impact and add value to the organization
Actively participate in regularly scheduled project review meetings, provide input to work plans or schedule issues, identify risks and project materials or vendors needed to support the project, and promptly inform project lead regarding environmental concerns, requirements, compliance issues, corrective measures, etc.
Conduct regular site inspections to assess compliance with the plan and permit requirements and monitor construction site’s environmental performance
Monitor, document and guide initiatives to minimize waste, avoid accidental releases or spills, and otherwise reduce potentially harmful releases to air, water, or soil
Assist the Grant Manager with grant proposals for air or sustainability activities
Act in accordance with Port Houston core values (respect, excellence, accountability, diligence, and you)
Manage and ensure compliance with TCEQ’s Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) or Corrective Action processes.
Asbestos abatement and disposal oversight and documentation.
Tier II hazardous chemical inventory reporting and coordination with internal departments.
Track and interpret regulatory updates from EPA, TCEQ, and other relevant agencies; assess implications for Port operations and permitting timelines.
Serve as the liaison with internal stakeholders and consultants to ensure timely, complete submittal of permit applications and environmental reports
Maintain documentation, correspondence logs, and project tracking in coordination with the Environmental Compliance Coordinator and project managers
Ensure delineation from Channel Marine Regulatory by coordinating, when necessary, on joint jurisdictional determinations but keeping this role focused strictly on upland and terrestrial environmental permitting responsibilities
Represent Port Houston in interagency meetings and public engagement forums on topics within this role’s scope
Act in accordance with Port Houston core values (respect, excellence, accountability, diligence, and you)
Perform related duties as required

Education/Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Ecology, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resource Management, or a closely related field
7+ years of progressive experience in environmental permitting, with a focus on state and federal land-based environmental regulatory compliance
Previous people-management experience required
In-depth understanding of:
Clean Water Act (404/401) as applied to land-based projects
NEPA, ESA, RCRA, CERCLA, TCEQ regulatory programs
Endangered Species Act and Migratory Bird Treaty Act
Experience coordinating with EPA, TCEQ, and local environmental agencies.
Master’s degree preferred
Certified Professional Environmental Auditor certification preferred for auditor function
Previous and comprehensive experience in permitting projects in conjunction with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
Ability to interpret environmental regulations, communicate permitting strategies, and manage consultants and timelines
Strong analytical, writing, and project management skills

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities And Behaviors

Strong knowledge of Clean Water Act (Sections 404, 401), NEPA, TCEQ, TGLO, EPA, ESA, MBTA, RCRA, CERCLA, and Clean Air Act.
Familiarity with TCEQ permitting programs (stormwater, air, waste, remediation)
Understanding of Nationwide and General Permits (as applicable to upland development)
Experience with Phase I, II, and III Environmental Site Assessments
Understanding of wetland delineation, habitat surveys, and ecological assessments
Ability to interpret and apply complex environmental regulations
Strong technical writing and verbal communication skills
Project management skills for tracking multiple permits and deadlines
Stakeholder engagement with agencies, consultants, and internal teams Critical thinking and environmental risk analysis
Competency in reviewing and editing environmental reports and permits
Ability to collaborate across departments and functions
Work independently and use sound judgment in permit planning
Adapt to evolving regulations and project needs
Maintain organized documentation and records
Coordinate consultants, contractors, and field teams for surveys or studies
Maintains integrity, professionalism, and confidentiality
Highly detail-oriented and organized
Shows initiative and takes ownership of responsibilities
Team-oriented and supportive of department goals
Excellent written and verbal communication skills as well as presentation skills
Computer skills to include Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint
Ability to mentor and support subordinates and promote a high degree of motivation
Ability to travel to attend conferences, meetings and workshops
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships
Ability to track and explain any differences in budget line items
Ability to interact comfortably with all levels of management
Attention to detail
A current, valid Texas driver's license is required
A Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC) must be obtained within 30 days of appointment, and be maintained for the duration of employment
Considered essential employees and may be required to work on holidays, evenings, nights, and be immediately recalled for emergencies at any time. They must remain available and "on call" 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, dependent on emergency

Key Competencies Required

Ethics and Values
Focus Group Efforts
Leadership Presence
Management Focus
Strategic Decision Making
Technical/Professional Knowledge and Skills
Cybersecurity Awareness and Collaboration
Innovation and Technology Adaptation

Port Houston Administration Building

added.title: EIR Environmental Scientist 1
added.description:
About Atlas

Atlas is a trusted leader in environmental and infrastructure consulting services; we provide services that enable communities to flourish and thrive. With a team of 3,500 employees and offices throughout the US, we combine local expertise and a network of relationships to deliver solutions to both public and private clients. Our services help improve the quality of life in the communities where we live and work. We always aim for smart, safe, and sustainable results. At Atlas we understand that our future is everyone’s responsibility, and we create a better experience at every stage of a project.

Job Description

Launch your career in environmental consulting by working on projects that help assess, clean up, and redevelop properties across the region. You'll gain hands-on experience in the field and office while learning from experienced professionals and making a meaningful impact on communities and the environment. We're looking for an enthusiastic, self-motivated individual who is eager to learn and grow. Success means developing strong technical skills, safely supporting field and office activities, and becoming a reliable member of our project team.

Core Responsibilities

Support environmental site investigations by collecting soil, groundwater, soil-vapor, and other environmental samples.
Conduct and document field activities, including soil borings, monitoring-well installations, and underground storage-tank excavations or removals.
Organize and evaluate sampling results using data tables, sample-location maps, and clear technical summaries.
Assist with proposals, work plans, environmental reports, permit applications, and site-specific health and safety plans.
Maintain accurate field notes, project records, and documentation in accordance with Atlas quality and safety practices.
Coordinate multiple assignments and communicate progress, field observations, and potential concerns to project team members.

You’ll thrive here if you have

A bachelor’s degree in geology, engineering, environmental science, or a related field.
Up to two years of relevant environmental consulting, field, laboratory, or academic experience. Georgia-specific experience is helpful but not required.
A strong commitment to performing fieldwork safely and producing accurate, well-documented work.
Technical, analytical, research, and problem-solving skills, with proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
The ability to communicate clearly, work independently with appropriate guidance, and contribute to a collaborative team.
A valid driver’s license and driving record that meet company requirements.
The ability to perform moderately strenuous field activities and travel overnight, primarily within the state, approximately 20% to 30% of the time.
Current 40-hour HAZWOPER training is preferred.

What You Can Expect From Us

The A-Team Experience is our employee program focused on helping our people thrive professionally, personally and as part of a community. We trust our people to do great work and live fulfilling lives, and we provide resources that care for our people, both at work and in life:

Health & Wellness: We offer medical, dental and vision coverage with multiple plan options, including no-cost employee-only medical coverage.
Time Off & Family Support: We offer vacation time, paid holidays, sick & safety leave (SSL) and paid parental leave
Retirement: We help employees plan for the future with a 401(k) and company match.
Insurance: To provide protection and peace of mind, we offer Life, AD&D (Accidental Death & Dismemberment) and Disability insurance.
Safety Program: We are committed to safety as part of our ‘quality of life’ core value, and we provide approved PPE at no cost and reimbursement for prescription safety glasses and protective footwear.
Learning & Development: We provide clear career paths, learning resources and development programs allowing you to see how you can grow and advance within the company. We offer internal certifications on specific skills and support external credentials through tuition reimbursement.
Belonging: We support Employee Communities (ECs), voluntary, employee-led groups that create connections, belonging and shared purposes.
Flexibility: May vary by project demands and regional workloads, but we are committed to providing reasonable accommodation to help employees manage their personal and professional responsibilities.

Our people and our culture are central to our work. Our values bring us together, create a sense of belonging and give us purpose. They guide how we make decisions, how we work as a team and how we serve our clients.

Life: We enhance the quality of life. We value people and safety above all else.
Heart: As our hallmark, we act with compassion, empathy, and respect.
Trust: We work together as partners, doing what we say with full accountability.
Mastery: Always striving for the highest quality, greatness inspires our work.

About The Job

Career Level: Entry
Employment Type: Full-time

EEO Statement

Atlas is committed to providing equal employment opportunities for all employees and applicants without regard to race (including hairstyles, hair texture, hair type, or hair length commonly or historically associated with race), ethnicity, creed, religion or religious creed, color, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, and related medical conditions or requests for pregnancy disability leave and/or family care leave), gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, citizenship or immigration status, primary language, crime victim status, criminal conviction history, uniformed service member or veteran status, marital status, age, genetic information, disability or protected medical condition, genetics, political affiliation or activities, or any other status protected under applicable federal, state, or local laws.

Notice to Third Party Agencies

Please note that Atlas Technical Consultants does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or employment agencies. In the absence of a signed Recruitment Fee Agreement, Atlas will not consider or agree to payment of any referral compensation or recruiter fee. In the event a recruiter or agency submits a resume or candidate without a previously signed agreement, Atlas explicitly reserves the right to pursue and hire those candidate(s) without any financial obligation to the recruiter or agency. Any unsolicited resumes, including those submitted to hiring managers, are deemed to be the property of Atlas.

Description

We are Accepting Applications for the Following Position:

Environmental Health County Manager
(10267)

Founded in the 1920s and headquartered in Decatur, GA, the DeKalb Public Health works to protect, promote and improve the health and well-being of all DeKalb County residents.

Our vision is for a healthier DeKalb where all residents have equitable access to public health resources and live healthy lives. If you have a passion for people and are looking to make an impact on the health of the community, we invite you to join our team! For more information about our agency please visit dekalbpublichealth.com.

POSTING DATE: 11/04/2026 APPLICATION DEADLINE: 12/04/2026

Exceptional Benefits Include

13 Paid Holidays
3 Weeks Annual Leave
3 Weeks Sick Leave
Flexible Schedules within our core working hours of M-F 8:15am-5pm
Pension Plan
Employer 401K Match
Payroll Deductible Health Benefits
Payroll Deductible Flex Benefits
Flexible Spending Accounts
Worksite Wellness
Diverse Workforce
Opportunities for Growth
Hybrid teleworking option for eligible positions after probation

LOCATION: Richardson Health Center

DIVISION/DEPARTMENT: Environmental Health

SALARY INFORMATION: $65,843.44 Annually / Pay Grade N / Job Code RCM010

Job Responsibilities

Under broad supervision, directs, manages, and evaluates countywide environmental health programs and personnel within the Division of Environmental Health. Provides leadership and oversight of regulatory, permitting, inspection, enforcement, and public health protection activities while ensuring compliance with applicable local, state, and federal laws, regulations, and policies. Serves as a technical expert, program administrator, and liaison to governmental agencies, regulated industries, community stakeholders, and the public.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Program Administration and Leadership

Directs, plans, develops, implements, and evaluates countywide environmental health programs and services, which may include retail food service, onsite sewage management, and vector control.
Develops, reviews, updates, and implements program policies, procedures, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Evaluates program performance, goals, and objectives and implements improvements to promote effective service delivery, operational efficiency, and regulatory compliance.
Assists with strategic planning, program development, resource allocation, and the establishment of program priorities.
Monitors program operations to ensure consistent service delivery and adherence to established standards.

Regulatory Compliance and Enforcement

Interprets, applies, and enforces applicable local, state, and federal environmental health laws, regulations, codes, and policies.
Directs and oversees plan reviews, permitting, inspections, monitoring, complaint investigations, and enforcement activities involving retail food service operations and other assigned environmental health programs.
Oversees administrative and legal enforcement actions, as appropriate, to address violations and protect public health.
Ensures consistent application of regulatory requirements, inspection standards, and compliance procedures across environmental health programs.
Provides guidance on complex regulatory matters and assists staff in resolving compliance issues.

Staff Management and Development

Supervises and manages a team of approximately three to four Environmental Health Specialists.
Provides leadership, training, mentoring, performance feedback, and daily work direction to assigned personnel.
Conducts performance evaluations and establishes expectations for employee performance and professional development.
Oversees staff development, continuing education, and in-service training activities.
Participates in recruitment, selection, employee discipline, and other personnel management activities.
Promotes accountability, teamwork, professional conduct, and consistent application of program standards.

Public Health Response and Investigations

Oversees investigations involving foodborne illness outbreaks, disease transmission, and other environmental health incidents.
Directs responses to environmental health emergencies, public health hazards, environmental nuisances, and citizen complaints.
Coordinates response activities with public health officials, healthcare providers, emergency management agencies, and state and federal partners.
Provides technical guidance and administrative oversight during environmental health incidents requiring coordinated public health intervention.
Ensures appropriate documentation, follow-up, and resolution of environmental health investigations.

Technical Consultation and Stakeholder Engagement

Provides technical guidance, regulatory interpretation, and professional consultation on environmental health matters.
Serves as a technical expert and advisor to staff, local governments, state and federal agencies, regulated industries, consultants, and the public.
Represents the Division before community organizations, professional associations, governmental bodies, committees, and public meetings.
Develops and maintains effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Communicates regulatory requirements, program expectations, and public health recommendations to diverse audiences.

Administrative Responsibilities

Oversees environmental health inspection, permitting, reporting, and data management systems.
Reviews and prepares program reports, recommendations, presentations, correspondence, and other administrative documents.
Monitors program activities and documentation to support operational accountability and regulatory compliance.
Performs other related duties as assigned.

Required Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Knowledge

Thorough knowledge of environmental health programs, regulatory processes, and public health protection principles.
Thorough knowledge of applicable environmental health laws, regulations, codes, policies, and enforcement procedures.
Comprehensive knowledge of management, supervision, strategic planning, and program evaluation.
Knowledge of public health emergency response, outbreak investigation, and risk communication practices.
Knowledge of environmental health inspection, permitting, monitoring, and compliance activities.

Skills And Abilities

Ability to interpret and apply complex laws, regulations, policies, and technical standards.
Ability to analyze complex problems, develop effective solutions, and make sound administrative and operational decisions.
Ability to plan, organize, direct, and evaluate environmental health programs and personnel.
Ability to promote compliance with public health laws, regulations, and established standards.
Ability to communicate effectively with diverse audiences, including governmental officials, regulated entities, professional organizations, employees, and the public.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with employees, community partners, public health officials, and other stakeholders.
Ability to interact effectively and professionally with individuals from diverse cultural, socioeconomic, educational, racial, ethnic, and professional backgrounds.
Ability to manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgment, and maintain accountability for program performance.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in Environmental Science, Biology, Chemistry, Geology, Engineering (Agricultural, Chemical, Civil, Environmental, Mechanical, or Sanitary), or a closely related field.

Four (4) years of professional experience in environmental health, environmental enforcement, environmental protection, environmental monitoring, environmental research, or a related regulatory field.
Reliable personal vehicle, valid driver's license, and ability to travel throughout the county as required.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Experience administering environmental health programs, regulatory compliance activities, and enforcement actions.

Three (3) or more years of supervisory or management experience in environmental health or public health regulatory programs.
Registration as a Registered Environmental Health Specialist (REHS) or Registered Sanitarian (RS).
Certified Retail Food Safety Manager (CFSM or CFPM).
Standardized Food Service Establishment Inspection Officer (Standardized) or Standardized Food Service Establishment Training and Inspection Officer (District Standard Trainer).
Completion of CDC's Vector Control for Environmental Health Professionals (VCEHP) Training.
Certified Septic Level 2 Inspector.

Working Environment

Work is performed primarily in an office and field environment within the county. The position requires frequent interaction with employees, regulated businesses, government agencies, community partners, and members of the public. Field responsibilities may include visits to food service establishments, onsite sewage systems, and other environmental health sites.

The work may involve exposure to outdoor weather conditions, potentially hazardous environments, infectious or communicable diseases, chemicals, pests, and other environmental health hazards. May require occasional evening, weekend, or emergency response duties based on operational needs.

The position requires the ability to travel throughout the county, conduct site visits and inspections, attend meetings, and respond to environmental health incidents as necessary. Employees must be able to perform the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.

Additional Information

NOTE:
Employment with DeKalb Public Health is not complete or official until applicants meet all pre-employment requirements. If this position requires a college degree and you are selected for an interview, you will be required to submit official transcripts to the Human Resources Department prior to any official offer of employment.

Not every applicant will receive an interview and only those selected for an interview will be notified. We have the right to close any position at any time.

Fingerprint Criminal Records Investigation Is Required

ALL APPLICANTS MUST APPLY FOR THIS POSITION & COMPLETE APPLICATION IN: ”Career Opportunities” at www.dph.georgia.gov

If you require accommodations under the American Disability Act (ADA), email request by the closing date of this announcement to: Brittany.leslie@dph.ga.gov

In addition to a competitive salary, we offer a generous benefits package that includes a flexible schedule, training opportunities, health insurance, employee retirement plan (ERS GSEPS), deferred compensation, 13 paid holidays, vacation & sick leave, paid parental leave, dental, vision, long term care, and life insurance.

Standard Benefits For Part-Time Employees

Part-time employees receive the Georgia Defined Contribution Plan and paid parental leave.

About the Role

Our client, a large organization in a regulated industry, is seeking an experienced CMMC Compliance Specialist
to lead its Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) effort. You will own the work of achieving and maintaining CMMC certification, which is essential to continuing and expanding the organization's business with federal agencies.
This is a hands-on, high-visibility role for someone who has stepped into environments with significant compliance gaps and driven them to a certification-ready state. You will assess current controls, build the remediation roadmap, and work with technical and business teams to close gaps against an established timeline.
You'll bring significant government contracting experience and a deep understanding of DFARS 252.204-7012, NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2, FedRAMP, and CMMC
.

Key Responsibilities

Program Planning:
Partner with the Project Manager to build and execute a comprehensive CMMC implementation plan, including scope, objectives, timelines, and resourcing. Maintain all required compliance documentation, including risk assessments, System Security Plans, and Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms).
Assessment Facilitation:
Lead assessments of cybersecurity practices, policies, and controls against CMMC requirements through documentation review, system owner interviews, and technical evaluation.
Gap Analysis:
Compare existing controls to CMMC and NIST SP 800-171 requirements, identify gaps, and prioritize recommendations to close them and reach certification.
Compliance Strategy:
Develop and drive the strategy to achieve and sustain compliance, including a risk-based approach to remediating deficiencies quickly and effectively.
Remediation Guidance:
Work with application, infrastructure, and security teams to build remediation plans, and advise on implementing appropriate controls and best practices.
Reporting:
Produce clear, detailed reports on findings, areas of non-compliance, vulnerabilities, and recommended remediation for both technical and executive audiences.
Training and Awareness:
Develop and deliver training sessions and workshops that connect everyday cybersecurity practices to CMMC requirements.
Continuous Improvement:
Track changes in regulations, standards, and the threat landscape, and keep controls and documentation current.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in IT, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field
7+ years of experience in IT/information security compliance, risk management, or a related field, preferably in a regulated industry
Significant government contracting experience
Hands-on experience with CMMC and/or FedRAMP
, along with working knowledge of NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2
and DFARS 252.204-7012

Demonstrated experience leading remediation and readiness efforts in environments with substantial compliance gaps
Experience conducting security assessments or audits
Proficiency in risk assessment methodologies
Strong analytical skills, with the ability to identify vulnerabilities and recommend practical solutions
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to work with stakeholders at all levels
Ability to think strategically while maintaining strong attention to detail
Ability to work independently and as part of a team

Preferred Qualifications

Certifications such as Certified CMMC Professional (CCP)
, Certified CMMC Assessor (CCA)
, CISSP
, CISM
, or CEH

Experience with FedRAMP authorization or continuous monitoring (a strong equivalent to direct CMMC experience, since CMMC is a relatively new framework)
Prior experience preparing an organization for a formal third-party or C3PAO assessment
